papers.title: A Unified Flexible Large Polysomnography Model for Sleep Staging and Downstream Clinical Screening
papers.summary: Presents LPSGM, a large PSG model trained on 220,500 hours from 16 public datasets, integrating domain-adaptive pretraining, flexible channel configurations, and a unified architecture for cross-center sleep staging and clinical screening. It achieved expert-level staging (kappa 0.845 vs inter-expert 0.850) and supported narcolepsy, OSA, and depression screening with AUCs up to 0.965 in transfer cohorts.

papers.title: NCEL: Convolution-Enhanced Lightweight Neural Architecture for Robust EEG Signal Decoding in Noninvasive Brain-Computer Interfaces.
papers.summary: Proposed NCEL, a lightweight neural architecture with a dynamic neural convolution module, multiscale temporal convolution branches, and channel-attention gating for robust EEG decoding. On five benchmark datasets, NCEL achieved 82.75% mean accuracy on BCIC IV-2b and outperformed EEGNet reference values by 12.53 percentage points on P300 and 9.54 points on BCIC IV-2b while using only ~0.008M parameters.

papers.title: RefineSleepNet: Task-Driven Signal-Domain Transformation for EEG/EOG Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Proposes RefineSleepNet, a sequence-to-sequence framework that first applies separate Signal Refinement U-Net branches to EEG and EOG waveforms preserving temporal length, then extracts epoch features with fusion and cross-epoch attention. Under subject-independent 10-fold cross-validation it reached accuracy/macro-F1 of 84.5%/79.8% on Sleep-EDF-39, 83.5%/78.1% on Sleep-EDF-153, and 80.3%/78.1% on ISRUC-3.

papers.title: CSPT-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Framework Integrating Center-Driven Sequence Supervision and Multimodal Pyramid Token Encoding.
papers.summary: Introduces CSPT-SleepNet, combining multimodal pyramid token encoding of EEG, EOG, and EMG with center-driven sequence supervision where non-center epochs receive weaker auxiliary labels. In subject-independent cross-validation it achieved accuracy/macro-F1 of 87.93%/83.53% on Sleep-EDF-20, 85.81%/80.87% on Sleep-EDF-78, and 84.06%/82.86% on ISRUC-S3, with center-driven supervision adding 0.60/0.91 points over equal-weight supervision.

papers.title: Physiology-Informed Blink Artefact Detection from Bilateral Frontal EEG Under Asymmetric Interference.
papers.summary: Develops a physiology-informed blink artifact detector for bilateral frontal EEG that combines waveform correlation, peak-time agreement, amplitude similarity, and symmetric-component dominance in an explicit rule without supervised model fitting. On ZuCo 1.0 scalp-pair data it achieved participant-mean precision 0.731, recall 0.774, and F1 0.734, with lower false-positive rates than single-channel thresholding and bilateral averaging.

papers.title: EOG Artifact Removal from EEG Using a Gated WGAN with Multi-Scale and Multi-Domain Feature Extraction.
papers.summary: Develops a gated, reconstruction-loss-assisted Wasserstein GAN (MDS-rarWGAN) with multi-scale and multi-domain feature extraction for single-channel EOG artifact removal from EEG. On EEGdenoiseNet it reached RRMSEs of 0.189 (time) and 0.183 (frequency) with correlation 0.955, and gated processing yielded the highest mean motor imagery classification accuracy among evaluated deep learning methods on BCI Competition IV 2a.

papers.title: Agentic EEG Pipeline Synthesis Using Large Language Models and the Model Context Protocol.
papers.summary: Presents an agentic framework in which an LLM orchestrator selects, parameterizes, and orders EEGLAB components via Model Context Protocol interfaces to synthesize task-specific EEG processing pipelines. On eight resting-state recordings, agent-generated pipelines achieved mean epoch retention 0.845 versus 0.843 for DISCOVER-EEG and mean SNR 13.92 dB versus 11.14 dB (interpreted cautiously due to differing filter boundaries).

papers.title: A Physiology-Informed Deep Learning Approach for Sleep-EEG Brain Age Estimation.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Developed a physiology-informed deep learning framework that estimates brain age from whole-night polysomnography, achieving a mean absolute error of 5.89 years across ~10,000 recordings from four cohorts and 5.41 years in independent external validation. Each 10-year increase in brain age gap was associated with 19% higher all-cause and 25% higher cardiovascular mortality risk, with learnable Gabor filters yielding spectral and sleep-stage readouts.

papers.title: MM-Net: A Multimodal Multi-Task Network for Sleep Staging and Sleep Apnea Assessment After Ischemic Stroke
papers.summary: Proposed MM-Net, a multimodal multi-task framework using cross-fitting and ridge-based embedding alignment to jointly perform sleep staging and respiratory-event detection from polysomnography after ischemic stroke. On iSLEEPS, it achieved 76.3% staging accuracy (κ = 0.656) and 0.825 respiratory-event AUC, and the aligned sleep-adapted encoder improved staging accuracy by 1.4 percentage points over a frozen encoder.

papers.title: Scalp EEG detects motor sequence replay signatures during wakeful rest
papers.summary: Tested whether ordered motor-sequence replay during wakeful rest can be detected from scalp EEG during motor skill learning, with conditions including targeted-memory reactivation (TMR). Neural states re-emerged in the practiced sequence order, indicating forward replay across conditions; accelerated TMR enhanced total learning, and stronger forward replay showed an exploratory relationship with micro-offline gains.

papers.title: Virtual EEG channel inference from four frontal electrodes for wearable EEG augmentation.
papers.summary: Developed FAVC-Net to infer 13 virtual EEG channels from four frontal electrodes using shared multi-scale encoding, source-state embeddings, GATv2 refinement, and attention-consistent skip fusion. Compared with the strongest non-FAVC baselines, it reduced log-spectral distance by 30.50% and PSD KL divergence by 38.94%, providing montage-compatible representations for low-channel EEG.

papers.title: Dynamic Evolution of Quantitative Electroencephalography During Graded Intracranial Hypertension and Screening of Candidate Early-Warning Features in a Rabbit Model.
papers.summary: Established a stepwise graded intracranial hypertension model in rabbits to compare quantitative EEG indices along a pressure gradient and screen early-warning features. The amplitude-integrated EEG lower margin declined earliest and was selected in five of six leave-one-rabbit-out folds, while theta and alpha power fell progressively with rising ICP.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Acoustic Stimulation of Slow Oscillations Using a Wireless EEG Headband: A Polysomnography-Validated Feasibility Study.
papers.summary: Tested closed-loop acoustic stimulation of slow oscillations using a wireless EEG headband with forehead electrodes in healthy participants, validated against simultaneous polysomnography. Phase targeting was consistent near the intended phase, and stimulation produced immediate enhancement of slow oscillations plus sustained increases in SO density and power in the 0.75-5 Hz range during deep sleep.

papers.title: Post-intervention high-beta synchronization tracks stable-manifold alignment during stick-balancing learning
papers.summary: Investigated learning-related changes in control dynamics and beta-band EEG during virtual stick balancing over two days in healthy adults. With practice, balance duration increased, distance to the stable manifold decreased, and post-intervention high-beta synchronization was inversely associated with that distance, suggesting it tracks the quality of transition from active correction to intrinsic control-OFF dynamics.

papers.title: FPGLNet: A Lightweight Frequency Prior-Gated Network for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed FPGLNet, a lightweight frequency prior-gated network for EEG emotion recognition combining mixed aggregation convolution, a Fourier convolution mixer, and prior-gated feedforward gating. It achieved classification accuracies of 96.22% and 92.69% on SEED-IV and SEED-V, respectively, balancing performance with reduced model complexity.

papers.title: How well does electrical source imaging reconstruct neural time series? Evidence from simultaneous scalp and intracranial EEG recordings
papers.summary: Assessed electrical source imaging (ESI) reconstruction of spontaneous neural time series using simultaneous high-density EEG and intracranial EEG in 34 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, comparing three distributed source models and one beamformer. Temporal reconstruction was limited (highest correlation 0.126) with localization errors around 3 cm and substantial spatial leakage, worsening with electrode depth and higher frequency; beamforming showed the weakest temporal reconstruction.

papers.title: Ketones and Sleep: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Preclinical Models, and Human Evidence.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and human evidence linking endogenous and exogenous ketosis to sleep architecture, quality, and sleep-disordered breathing. It reports that acetoacetate, but not β-hydroxybutyrate, increases slow-wave activity during NREM sleep and suppresses glutamate release in mice, while human findings are suggestive but heterogeneous (e.g., acute carbohydrate restriction increasing slow-wave sleep and reducing REM), concluding that ketone effects on sleep are conditional rather than universally sleep-promoting.

papers.title: EEG-Based Decoding of Musical Mode and Melodic Direction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
papers.summary: Proposes an Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) feature-extraction framework that decomposes EEG recorded during active piano performance and trains a Wide Neural Network on energy descriptors from the first four IMFs to decode musical mode and melodic direction. Reports average accuracies of 84% (intra-subject) and 81% (inter-subject, first IMF) with AUC-ROC of ~0.9, and robustness to handedness.

papers.title: A Knowledge Transfer Method from Multi-Channel to Single-Channel EEG Toward Real-World Emotion Recognition Deployment.
papers.summary: This study proposes a multi-channel-to-single-channel knowledge transfer framework using a 32-channel teacher and a sparsely gated student trained with classification, logits distillation, frequency-band consistency, and gating regularization losses, with retraining on the locked physical channel. On DEAP binary Arousal and Valence classification with 32-fold leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, it achieved higher subject-averaged balanced accuracy and F1-score than a channel-matched cross-entropy baseline.

papers.title: DSGTANet: A semi-supervised dual-stream graph-temporal adaptation network for cross-subject continuous EEG emotion recognition.
papers.summary: Develops DSGTANet, a semi-supervised dual-stream graph-temporal adaptation network combining a learnable-graph spatial stream, a Transformer temporal stream, and reliability-driven uncertainty-weighted fusion and alignment for cross-subject continuous EEG emotion recognition. On a newly collected 40-participant dynamic-emotion dataset and DEAP, it reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in valence and arousal regression.

papers.title: Auditory tracking magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution during wakefulness and propofol-based anesthesia in human sEEG
papers.summary: Used stereoelectroencephalography in 13 epilepsy patients to jointly characterize auditory tracking magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution during wakefulness versus propofol-based anesthesia. Anesthesia reduced stimulus-rate power and phase alignment, weakened the distance-response relationship from Heschl's gyrus, and lowered acoustic-envelope decoding accuracy in contrastive learning (CEBRA) embeddings.

papers.title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate EEG Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.summary: Examined resting-state EEG spectral, aperiodic, and microstate features in multiple sclerosis using age-adjusted models with FDR correction, finding significant diagnosis associations for global bandwidth, global aperiodic offset, and offset at all 128 channels. Because MS and control age ranges did not overlap, the authors caution the diagnosis effect depends on extrapolation and remains exploratory.

papers.title: STDR-Net: A Spatio-Temporal Dependency Refinement Network for Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
papers.summary: Proposes STDR-Net, a spatio-temporal dependency refinement network that recalibrates convolutional tokens, models global interactions, restores local representations via a cross-stage residual bridge, and refines fused sequences with a bidirectional LSTM. It achieved accuracies of 82.69%, 86.99%, and 59.76% on BCI IV-2a, IV-2b, and PhysioNet, respectively, with the highest observed mean accuracy on IV-2a but non-significant gains on IV-2b after multiplicity correction.

papers.title: Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection
papers.summary: Investigates normative-deviation modeling for EEG-based major depressive disorder detection, training healthy-control reference models and integrating scalar-level (S-NDD) or feature-level (F-NDD) deviations with deep EEG representations, plus target healthy-control-assisted score calibration for cross-source evaluation. Experiments on two public datasets report effectiveness across subject-independent within-source and bidirectional cross-source settings.

papers.title: EEG-guided robotic control of transcranial magnetic stimulation
papers.summary: Develops an EEG-guided robotic TMS method in which a pre-trained CNN classifies resting state versus right- or left-hand movement from 2-s EEG segments to automatically control both stimulus timing and robotic coil location. In a proof-of-concept study, decoding required 150 ms and the robot moved from vertex to motor targets in 7.5 s, enabling closed-loop brain-state-dependent control of stimulation site.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.summary: Systematically reviews deep learning computational approaches for EEG analysis in neurological disease diagnosis, covering CNN, RNN, hybrid, GAN, LLM, autoencoder, and transformer architectures for modeling spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal dynamics across epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related disorders, alongside preprocessing, denoising, and clinical-translation challenges.

papers.title: MTFNet: A Lightweight Multi-Scale Time-Frequency Neural Network for Multi-Class Event Recognition in DAS-Based Perimeter Security.
papers.summary: Proposes MTFNet, a lightweight parallel time-frequency dual-branch network that directly processes 1D DAS signals using a 1D Inception-ResNet time branch and a multi-scale spectral frequency branch with attention-free fusion. On a self-built five-class perimeter security dataset it achieved 99.55% accuracy with 0.12 M parameters and maintained 94.06% accuracy at 0 dB SNR.

papers.title: Scalable hardware and software for high-density, multi-regional electrophysiology in non-human primates
papers.summary: Presents MIND, a lightweight implantable microdrive supporting multiple independently positioned Neuropixels probes for chronic multi-regional recordings, paired with UnitAssay, an automated spike-sorting curation framework. Tested in rhesus macaques across parietal, prefrontal, and motor cortices during reaching and eye-movement tasks, the platform enabled stable multi-probe recordings and improved single-unit identification over Kilosort 4 labels and standard SpikeInterface quality control.

papers.title: EEG-Based Machine Learning Classification of Shooting Conditions and Performance Levels During the Shooting Preparation Stage.
papers.summary: Using EEG from 35 shooters, the study classified shooting conditions (normal, noise, low-light) and performance levels (high vs. low) with machine learning. FBCSP+SVM achieved 91% accuracy for normal vs. low-light and 81% for high vs. low performance within-dataset, but leave-one-subject-out cross-validation accuracies were only 59–70%, indicating limited cross-subject generalization.

papers.title: EEG Features of Cortical Intent for Urination and Defecation in Healthy Aging and Spinal Cord Injury: A Descriptive Feasibility Study for BCI Neurorehabilitation.
papers.summary: The study characterized EEG spatiotemporal dynamics and cortical reorganization during motor intentions for urination and defecation in healthy young/older adults and spinal cord injury (SCI) patients. All groups showed sensorimotor event-related desynchronization (ERD), with healthy older adults exhibiting greater beta2 ERD during SUD than young adults, and functional connectivity analysis revealed enhanced long-range frontal connectivity in aging and SCI, suggesting compensatory reorganization.

papers.title: Association Between EEG Activity and Motor Imagery Ability in Single-Joint Movements: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory pilot study examined associations between motor imagery ability (KVIQ scores) and EEG oscillatory activity during single-joint wrist dorsiflexion imagery in 11 healthy adults. Kinesthetic KVIQ scores were negatively correlated with 6.5–13 Hz activity at O1 during kinesthetic motor imagery (p=0.024, r=-0.869), and visual KVIQ scores were positively correlated with post-task 10–16.5 Hz activity at F7 during visual motor imagery (p=0.023, r=0.937).

papers.title: Procalcitonin and C-Reactive Protein Are Elevated at the Threshold of Cortical Electrocerebral Silence but Do Not Track Graded EEG Severity in Critically Ill Children: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 97 critically ill children, procalcitonin and C-reactive protein were markedly elevated at the threshold of cortical electrocerebral silence (Synek grade 5) compared to preserved cortical activity, but within Synek grades 1-4 neither biomarker showed a graded association with EEG severity, nor did they correlate with spectral qEEG metrics.

papers.title: Overt and Covert Speech-State Classification from Tripolar Concentric Ring Electrode EEG: A 4 mm and 10 mm Configuration Study.
papers.summary: The study applied small 4 mm tripolar concentric ring electrodes (TCREs) for EEG recording of overt and covert speech in 16 participants, comparing 4 mm and 10 mm configurations. EEGNet achieved the highest mean classification accuracy (84.06±15.57%), followed by SVM (81.56±14.23%) and LDA (76.56±15.30%), and overt speech produced higher task-to-baseline ratios than covert speech.

papers.title: Multimodal Neurorehabilitation Including Auditory EEG Neurofeedback: A Proof of Concept Tested After Resection of a Giant Olfactory Groove Meningioma.
papers.summary: A 53-year-old man who underwent resection of a giant olfactory groove meningioma completed a 4-week multimodal neurorehabilitation program including auditory SMR/theta EEG neurofeedback, showing improvements in global cognition, executive function, verbal recall, functional independence, and mobility, alongside reduced theta power and increased SMR/beta power and altered connectivity.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction in depression: dual-task event-related potentials and task-phase-dependent EEG functional connectivity.
papers.summary: Compared 30 patients with depression and 30 matched controls using dual-task ERP and task-phase-dependent EEG imaginary-coherence functional connectivity across resting, face-perception (N170), and face mismatch-conflict (N270) phases. Depression showed prolonged N170 latency with reduced amplitude, prolonged N270 latency with increased amplitude, and task-phase-dependent multi-frequency network imbalances; longer N170/N270 latencies correlated with more severe depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Network-Resolved and Frequency-Specific EEG-fMRI Representational Similarity Analysis of Visual Imagery.
papers.summary: Using EEG-fMRI representational similarity analysis with the Schaefer atlas, the study found significant model-brain correspondence in the visual network during visual perception but not during visual imagery, and revealed frequency- and time-dependent cross-modal correspondences between EEG time-frequency representations and fMRI network representations involving multiple functional networks during visual imagery.

papers.title: Reduced cognitive empathy and differences in EEG activity in low-achieving adolescents.
papers.summary: Compared 40 adolescents aged 14-17 with low versus adequate academic achievement using the Basic Empathy Scale, a facial-expression recognition test, and EEG recordings. The low-achieving group showed significantly lower cognitive empathy in the primary between-group analysis, with no significant overall difference in facial emotion recognition accuracy and only exploratory between-group differences in source-level oscillatory EEG activity.

papers.title: EEG reflects subjective but not behavioral hearing in noise performance.
papers.summary: Compared three measures of hearing in noise (tone-in-noise detection, speech reception threshold, self-reported SSQ) against auditory brainstem responses, cortical EEG, FM detection, and self-report. FM detection was a common predictor across all models, whereas EEG P3 amplitude was retained only for the subjective SSQ model, suggesting cortical EEG relates more to subjective than behavioral hearing in noise.

papers.title: Tablet-Camera Iris Landmarks and EEG/PPG-Derived Arousal Indices During Naturalistic Reading: Geometric Confounding and Exploratory Within-Subject Associations.
papers.summary: Evaluated whether MediaPipe iris landmark distances from a tablet camera estimate EEG- and PPG-derived arousal markers during naturalistic reading in 48 participants (43,923 30-s windows). Raw iris distances correlated only weakly with EEG alpha/theta, but face scale explained 93% of their variance; after normalizing for face width, adjusting for ocular luminance and head pose, and using within-subject Ridge regression, the alpha association was nonsignificant (r=+0.021, p=0.33; group mean r=+0.078, p=0.07), indicating the landmark distance does not validate as a pupil or arousal measure.

papers.title: How Aesthetic and Economic Factors Affect Consumers' Purchasing Decisions: Evidence from EEG.
papers.summary: Used ERP recordings from 70 Chinese university students making purchase/rejection decisions on artworks in a 2x2 aesthetic-valence by price design to test how aesthetic and economic factors jointly drive purchasing. Aesthetic valence had a larger effect than price (ηp2=0.662 vs 0.246), and medial frontal negativity amplitude and theta-band power were larger during purchase than rejection, most pronounced when buying negatively rated artworks.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
